summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy, was admitted for an acute exacerbation characterized by over 20 daily watery bowel movements, left upper quadrant abdominal pain, and fevers. He was started on IV methylprednisolone and IV fluids for dehydration, which improved his creatinine from 1.3 to 1.0. Abdominal imaging showed stable bowel wall thickening at the anastomosis site and new splenomegaly. A repeat X-ray suggested possible partial obstruction, but CT ruled out perforation or abscess. Stool studies were negative for infection. The patient developed steroid-induced anxiety, managed with Seroquel. He insisted on discharge against medical advice on hospital day 5, after showing some improvement with reduced bowel movements. He was discharged on prednisone, azathioprine, Protonix, opium tincture, and Seroquel, with follow-up arranged in GI and primary care clinics.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
